sources.title: datayoda/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-hipfire-MQ4 · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: A quantized hipfire snapshot of Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune, measured on a 20 GB AMD RX 7900 XT. On the same card and model weights, it prefills 1.44-1.85× faster than the Q4_K_S GGUF on llama.cpp and decodes ~24% faster — 36.5 tok/s on real prompts with the bundled MTP head accepted at τ≈1.94 tokens/step.

sources.title: Swift 1.5 Qwen3.8-27B | UkisAI
sources.snippet: The results below compare Qwen3.8-27B, the foundation base model, Swift 1.0, the first UkisAI adaptation, and Swift 1.5. All three use the same saved evaluation protocols, and every score is a final five-repeat aggregate.

sources.title: Swift — shorter thinking | UkisAI
sources.snippet: Swift-Qwen3.8-27B is UkisAI's reasoning-efficient derivative of Qwen3.8-27B, using 58.3% fewer thinking tokens while maintaining near-identical performance (<1% loss) and as a result getting a x1.95 speed-up on several tasks. Read the model report. See live download counts.

sources.title: Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF · Models
sources.snippet: Through fine-tuning, a model can be trained on a small amount of data to target a specific dataset. Completing this step allows you to learn about dataset creation, configuring the model environment, LoRA fine-tuning, dataset optimization, and model hyperparameter optimization, among other things.
